plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid (profitable), and you pay only the second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you're the highest). Bidding above or below true value only risks either winning at a loss or missing profitable wins. Since this is a one-shot round with no repeated interaction to exploit collusion, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid, bidding above my value risks overpaying, and bidding below risks losing profitable wins. With no prior history to suggest collusion or irrational behavior, the optimal strategy is straightforward: bid exactly my valuation of $33 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do, since the payment depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth if I win with a high second-highest bid, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my true value of $31 to maximize expected profit.
